Resolves #21514

neo-dark's error, alert and info states get their colors. The ten palette steps the theme read but never defined now exist, and the twelve semantic names and one cyberpunk name that pointed at nothing now read the existing token with the same role. A new guard, `check-theme-var-references`, fails a commit or PR that adds a fallback-free `var()` nothing defines. On `origin/dev` it reports exactly this ticket's 23 names; on this branch, and on `origin/dev` plus this branch's theme files, it reports none.

Evidence: L3 (headless Chromium probes of the real examples and `apps/form` for AC-1, AC-2 and AC-4; the guard runs in lint-staged and the PR baseline job, its spec in CI) → L3 required (AC-1 and AC-2 are rendered colors). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | outside-CI: `examples/form/validation` in neo-dark, email `jane.doe@`, then Tab. Error text and border: `rgb(240, 241, 244)` on dev, `rgb(255, 138, 128)` here; the text is `rgb(255, 255, 255)`. Same on the invalid state of `examples/form/field/text` (frames). `apps/form` (dev's version overlaid locally; it opens in neo-dark): an invalid phone `12ab` goes from `rgb(240, 241, 244)` to `rgb(255, 138, 128)`. A half-typed required email shows the alert color `rgb(255, 171, 64)` instead, because the app opts into `useAlertState` and that field counts as empty (pre-existing, defect-note `78df7b44`). |
| AC-2 | outside-CI: `examples/component/statusbadge` and `examples/component/toast` in neo-dark. On dev the alert, error and info badges and the danger toast have no background, and their text is the text color. Here: alert `#6E4D24` with white, error `#3D2828` with `#FFE8E6`, info `#242F41` with `#E6EFFF`, danger toast `#251B1D` with `#FFE8E6`. |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/checkThemeVarReferences.spec.mjs` (live-tree control plus each failure direction) and the PR baseline row `theme var references`. The scratch-edit failure is under Test Evidence. |
| AC-4 | outside-CI: the frames below, from the evidence branch `ada/21514-evidence`. |

## Deltas from ticket

- **Seeds.** Red is the theme's existing error red `#FF8A80` (Material Red A100). Blue is `#82B1FF` (Blue A100). Orange `#FFAB40` (Orange A200) and yellow `#FFE57F` (Amber A100) replace their A100 neighbours, which darken to khaki and olive. Every other step is a `color-mix` toward `--white` (100: 20 % seed) or `--gray-900` (600 to 900: 80, 40, 20 and 10 %), so the dark surfaces keep the theme's own undertone. The ticket asked to derive the steps like the theme's existing scales. The green scale is SCSS `lighten`/`darken` output, and in Chromium its 50 to 200 steps compute to white and its 900 step to black (out of scope, noted in defect-note `ff51b4cb`), so I did not copy it.
- `--selectfield-error-color` now reads `var(--red-500)` instead of repeating `#ff8a80`, so the two field reds cannot drift. No visible change.
- **Semantic names**, corrected to the existing token with the same role (January's precedent: correct the name, add no token):

  | Theme | Was | Now | Why this token |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | neo-dark, neo-light | `--sem-color-text-neutral-disabled` | `--sem-color-text-disabled` | neo-dark's `button/Base.css` already used it for secondary text |
  | neo-dark, neo-light | `--sem-color-icon-neutral-disabled` | `--sem-color-text-disabled` | the same file's glyph colors read text tokens |
  | neo-dark, neo-light | `--sem-color-text-primary-contrast` | `--sem-color-text-neutral-contrast` | the active text of the secondary and ghost uis |
  | neo-dark, neo-light | `--sem-color-surface-neutral-contrast` | `--sem-color-bg-neutral-contrast` | the bg family's contrast step; nothing in `src` reads `--cmp-tooltip-bg` yet |
  | neo-dark | `--sem-color-bg-subtle` (6 sites) | `--sem-color-bg-neutral-highlighted`; the week and month weekend fills mix it at 35 % alpha | the theme's highlighted step, `--gray-800`; weekend fills stay translucent like every other theme's, so the week view's hour lines show |
  | neo-dark | `--sem-color-text-primary-highlighted` | `--sem-color-fg-primary-highlighted` | the fg family's highlighted step |
  | neo-dark | `--sem-color-bg-hover` (footer buttons) | `--sem-color-surface-neutral-hover` | the dark twin of neo-light's 5 % footer hover overlay |
  | neo-light | `--sem-color-bg-neutral-strong` (footer) | `--sem-color-bg-neutral-default` | neo-dark's footer token |
  | cyberpunk | `--cyber-yellow` | `--cyber-gold` | the theme's only yellow |

- **Visible side effects.** In neo-dark these were all transparent. The calendar's week and month weekend columns now get a translucent `--gray-800` band (35 % alpha, so the week view's hour lines stay visible). The year view's week column, the calendar settings header, and the docs members list and parameter table header now read `--gray-800` (calendar frames below). The neo-light footer now paints `#FAFAFA` over the page's `#FCFCFC`, which looks the same as before.

## Test Evidence

Every new pairing clears WCAG: badge text 11.7:1 (error) and 11.6:1 (info), white on the alert badge 7.6:1, danger toast 14.2:1, error text on `--gray-900` 8.4:1, process arrow on `--gray-900` 3.3:1 (non-text, 3:1 needed).

AC-3's scratch edit was a real commit attempt that added `--selectfield-hint-color : var(--red-450);`. HEAD did not move, and the edit was reverted:

```
✖ node ./buildScripts/util/check-theme-var-references.mjs:
    [undefined] theme-neo-dark reads --red-450, which nothing defines: theme-neo-dark/form/field/Select.css:7
husky - pre-commit script failed (code 1)
```

All 26 component tokens this PR touches were also read at a theme root with every current sheet of the theme linked. On dev, 25 resolve to nothing; the 26th, `--selectfield-error-color`, was a literal. Here all 26 resolve. (The process tokens have no rendered consumer today, because both process examples pass their own `arrowColor`.)

## Addressed Review Feedback

Responding to review https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/21516#pullrequestreview-5984554708:

**Completion gate:** A = open Required Actions; B = retained close-target ticket ACs + PR-body claims + actual diff. A is empty relative to B at this head.

- [x] **`[ADDRESSED]`** Use a translucent token (such as `var(--sem-color-surface-neutral-hover)`, matching `FooterContainer.css` and the `.35`-alpha `rgba(...)` weekend fills in `theme-neo-light` and `theme-dark`) for `--c-w-weekend-background-color` in `resources/css/theme-neo-dark/calendar/view/week/Component.css:12` (and align `--c-m-weekend-background-color` in `resources/css/theme-neo-dark/calendar/view/month/Component.css:8` if keeping Week and Month weekend shading consistent) so `.neo-c-w-column.neo-weekend` does not paint over `.neo-c-w-column-container`'s `linear-gradient` horizontal hour lines (`src/calendar/view/week/Component.mjs:325-330`), and refresh `calendar-week.png` to confirm the Sunday/Saturday hour rules remain visible.
      **Commit:** 013993d76a
      **Details:** The week and month weekend fills now read `color-mix(in srgb, var(--sem-color-bg-neutral-highlighted) 35%, transparent)`. That is the same role token at the 35 % alpha the other themes use. I chose it over the hover token so that a static band does not change when someone tunes hover. Measured in neo-dark, both compute to `color(srgb 0.157 0.173 0.216 / 0.35)`. The refreshed `calendar-week.png` shows every hour line in the Sunday and Saturday columns, and the new `calendar-month.png` shows the month view. The year view's week column stays opaque, as it is in `theme-light` and `theme-dark`.

Your two watch notes on the guard, kept as they are:
- A `var(--x)` inside a quoted string would be a loud false positive: the commit fails and its author sees why. It cannot be a silent miss, so I did not strip strings.
- `--x: var(--x)` is a cycle. That is a different class from "a name nothing defines", which is the class the docblock scopes the guard to. None exists today.

Facts corrected in the body: the calendar frames, the side-effects line and the `--sem-color-bg-subtle` row now describe the translucent weekend fill (they said opaque `--gray-800`), and the commit list names 013993d76a.

All Required Actions are discharged against B at this head. CI is running on 013993d76a; I re-request your review at green.
